input: if I needed a filling how long would it take?
reply: Thirty to forty-five minutes depending on the tooth [1, 2].

chunks.text:
- Check-up: 20 minutes
- Hygienist: 30 minutes
- Extended hygienist (first visit or heavy staining): 45 minutes
- Filling: 30 to 45 minutes depending on the tooth
- Emergency assessment: 20 minutes

Thirty to forty-five minutes depending on the tooth. Local anaesthetic in most cases, though very
small fillings sometimes do not need it.

Afterwards the numbness lasts two to four hours. Avoid chewing on that side until it has gone —
it is easy to bite the inside of your cheek without noticing.

One or two appointments, each 60 to 90 minutes. The infected tissue is removed, the canals are
cleaned and shaped, and the space is filled and sealed. A tooth that has had root canal treatment
usually needs a crown afterwards to stop it fracturing.

£145 to £260. The range reflects the size of the filling and which tooth it is; back teeth take
longer and cost more. The exact figure is given after examination, before anything starts.

teeth that feel loose. Bleeding gums are not normal, and are usually the earliest sign.
